intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Bradley County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated November 19, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Banks
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer A review of the Town's payroll records revealed Internal Revenue Service (IRS) quarterly 941 reports were not prepared, and the Town did not remit payroll withholdings for reporting periods dating back to 2020. On September 26, 2025, the Town remitted $2,549 to the IRS for 2018 and on September 29, 2025, the Town remitted $2,689 to the IRS for 2019. A similar finding was noted in the previous report.

cities.name: Warren
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor The City did not solicit competitive bids for the purchase of two police vehicles costing $43,855 each, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58-303.
